title: Why Is Water Condensing on the Inside of My Windows?

seo.title: Why Is Water Condensing on the Inside of My Windows?
seo.meta_description: Interior window condensation forms when humid indoor air reaches glass cold enough to fall below the dew point. High humidity and cold glass make it worse.
seo.search_intent: Resolve the household problem clearly and safely by identifying likely causes and practical next steps.

excerpt: Water on the room side of a window is often not a window leak at all. It is indoor water vapor turning into liquid on a cold surface.
content_html:
Condensation forms when humid indoor air reaches a surface colder than the air's dew point. Windows are often among the coldest interior surfaces, so they are where the first visible droplets appear.

Two variables matter: humidity and glass temperature

The more moisture the air contains, the less cold the glass needs to be before condensation begins. Poorer insulating performance and colder outdoor weather both lower the interior glass temperature.

Why it is often worse in the morning

Overnight, a closed bedroom gains moisture from breathing and may cool slightly. Heavy curtains close to the glass can also reduce warm room-air circulation at the window.

Showers, cooking, and indoor drying contribute

Moisture produced in one room moves through the house. A poorly exhausted shower can show up later as droplets on a bedroom window.

Condensation is not the same as a leak

Uniform droplets across the room-side glass point toward condensation. Water entering at the frame during rain, localized wall staining, or moisture unrelated to indoor humidity and temperature deserves investigation for leakage.

Fog between panes is a different problem

If an insulated double-pane unit fogs inside the sealed space where you cannot wipe it from either side, the window seal may have failed.

Where the droplets form adds information

Condensation concentrated near glass edges may simply mark the coldest parts of the assembly. If it appears only behind a closed blind or heavy curtain, improve air circulation there before assuming the entire window needs replacement.

Colder outdoor weather changes the threshold

The same indoor humidity that caused no condensation in fall may create droplets during a much colder night. A home can therefore start showing wet windows even when indoor moisture production has not increased.

The window is showing the relationship between indoor humidity and surface temperature. Lowering moisture, warming the surface, or both is the basis of prevention.

faq.question: Does condensation mean my window is leaking?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Even droplets on the indoor glass are often condensed indoor moisture.

faq.question: Why is it worse in the morning?
faq.answer: Bedrooms can gain moisture overnight while the glass is especially cold.

faq.question: What if the fog is between two panes?
faq.answer: That can indicate a failed seal in an insulated glass unit.
